references.text: Moses appointed Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites as cities of refuge.
Parallel text describing the same three cities of refuge east of the Jordan: Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan, appointed by Moses.
God's command to give six cities of refuge to the Levites, which is the basis for the cities mentioned in Joshua 20:8.
Specifies that three cities of refuge were to be on the east side of the Jordan, corresponding to Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan.
Golan in Bashan from the half-tribe of Manasseh is mentioned as a Levitical city, the same city as the place of refuge in Joshua 20:8.
Bezer from the tribe of Reuben is mentioned as a Levitical city, the same city as the place of refuge in Joshua 20:8.
Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad is mentioned as a Levitical city and place of refuge, the same as in Joshua 20:8.
Ramoth in Gilead is mentioned as an important city, the same location as the city of refuge in Joshua 20:8.
